$schema_note: ONE definition of which guards must have a published verdict, read by both
languages. Python publishes from ETL/lib/guard_verdicts.py; TypeScript reads
it in website/frontend/scripts/check_verdicts.ts. A second copy of this list
would drift the first time either side gained a guard, which is the defect
this repo keeps finding (see ETL/schema/check_cross_language_constants.py).
Fields:
id        the verdict's key. Stable; renaming one loses its history.
cadence   'weekly'    the ETL cron publishes it, so it can be LATE:
SILENT is enforced against the observed spacing.
'on_change' a credentialled run publishes it. It has no clock to
be late against, so SILENT is not enforced. It goes
red two other ways: DRIFTED when the code it judges
changes, and STALE when the CORPUS moves past it.
needs     what the guard cannot run without, and LOAD-BEARING: a guard
that names a store here is answering a question about DATA, so
its verdict is void once the corpus moves, whatever its cadence.
Three of the four on_change guards judge live Postgres and no
fingerprinted file changes when a call closes, so without this
their verdicts would have covered today's corpus forever.
Derived from, not duplicated -- do not add a 'reads_corpus' flag
that can disagree with the credentials the guard actually needs.
code      repo-relative paths whose content the verdict is bound to. A
verdict produced against a different hash of these is DRIFTED.
For a weekly guard this is what makes 'the container is running
last week's code' visible; for an on_change guard it is the
whole enforcement mechanism.
refresh   the exact command that produces a fresh verdict. Printed in the
failure, because a guard that says 'stale' without saying how to
fix it gets muted.
command   present only where ETL/lib/guard_verdicts.py drives the guard
and publishes for it. A guard that publishes its OWN verdict
(the TypeScript ones do, because they have real figures to
carry) has no command here: two ways to publish one verdict is
two things to keep in step.
tolerate  exit codes that mean 'worth saying out loud, not worth failing
over'. Named per guard, never inferred from the number.
code_suffixes  narrows what a named directory contributes to the hash.

$why: Where a reader without credentials gets the verdicts. The site already
holds DATABASE_URL because the product cannot work without it; that is a
credential we cannot avoid having. A DATABASE_URL secret in GitHub
Actions is one we can, and it would widen a compromised workflow from
'can read our code' to 'can read and write every award we hold'.
Override with GUARD_FEED_URL to point at a preview deployment or a local
`next dev`; nothing in an automatic path may need that override.
Guards that run only when a human types the command, each with the reason
it cannot be wired and a date by which that reason must be re-examined.
Read by ETL/schema/check_guard_reachability.py, which fails the build on a
check_* module that is in neither an automatic path nor this block -- and
fails again once a `review` date passes, so the block cannot quietly become
the place orphans are kept.
Every entry below was found by an audit on 2026-08-08, not by a failure.
Two of them were RED at the moment they were found, which is the cost of
the arrangement they are recording.
`npm run check` is not an automatic path. It is the command whose serial
chain stopped at link 14 of 27 all week.

check_country_gates.reason: Declares DATABASE_URL `optional` and prints 'nothing to check' without it, so putting it in CI would buy a green step that reads nothing -- the precise defect the verdict channel exists to remove. check_gate_field_reach.reason: Same shape as check_country_gates: DATABASE_URL is `optional` and its absence yields a vacuous pass, so CI is the wrong home and the verdict channel is the right one. Green when run against Postgres on 2026-08-08 (3061 comparators over 23 fields).

check_answer_reach.reason: Third of the same shape as check_country_gates and check_gate_field_reach: DATABASE_URL is `optional` and its absence yields a vacuous pass, so a CI step would buy a green tick over a run that graded nothing. It is worse than the other two if wired, because it also refuses to report a verdict about a table the LEXICAL index ordered -- so in CI, where there is no VOYAGE_KEY, the one thing it exists to observe is the one thing it cannot see. Runs in `npm run check` against the corpus, which is where it is meaningful. Declared manual rather than wired on 2026-08-09; ETL/schema/check_guard_reachability.py was RED on main naming it, alongside three genuinely hermetic checks that were wired the same day.

check_gate_subject.reason: Needs DATABASE_URL and runs inside `make eligibility`, the publish target it guards; there is no automatic publish for it to attach to. Its layer-1 assertions are free, so it is a candidate for the weekly cron rather than a permanent manual.

check_fetched_text_leaks.reason: Reads data/raw/scheme_enrichment/found_*.json, which is gitignored, and no CI step in this repo may depend on gitignored data; the weekly Railway cron does not have the fetch files either. So unlike the five above this one is not manual for want of a credential -- there is no automatic runner that can see its input at all. It is not left to a human remembering: load_scheme_text.py calls scan() on exactly the files it is about to load and REFUSES TO WRITE on an active-set hit, so the check runs at the one moment fetched text becomes corpus. Skipping needs --skip-leak-check, typed. Review is for whether that in-loader call is still the only entry point once a fetch pipeline exists that CI can see.

Runs in `npm run check` today; it belongs on the verdict channel as an `on_change` guard, which is where a credentialled check reaches a credential-free reader.

accepted.$why: A failure somebody has already diagnosed, written down and routed to a person. check_verdicts.ts is the READOUT of the guards that hold credentials, and on 2026-08-12 three of them were red for reasons already decided -- which made `npm run check` red on every branch in the repository, including branches touching nothing any of them watches. A signal no branch can turn green is a signal people learn to step over, and then it stops catching the fourth guard, the one nobody had looked at. So the readout separates FAILING from FAILING FOR A REASON SOMEBODY ACCEPTED. What keeps this from being a mute button is enforced in acceptance() and nowhere else, so it cannot mean two things: an entry is bound to a specific FAILURE (a regex the guard's own summary must match, so a guard that starts failing a different way still reaches a person), it covers DEGRADED only (the other statuses say the reader does not know what the guard would find, and not knowing is what this channel exists to remove), it EXPIRES on its review date, it fails the build once the guard it covers goes GREEN (an acceptance that outlives what it accepted is pre-authorisation for the next regression under the same wording), and an acceptance naming an unregistered guard fails too (nothing would ever read it). Held failures are printed in full on every run: an acceptance nobody sees is indistinguishable from a check that never looked. THE BLOCK IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY. It was built on 2026-08-12 for three red guards and then not used for any of them, because each turned out to have a real fix or a dated end -- the mechanism exists for a failure that is genuinely someone's standing decision, not as somewhere to put today's inconvenience.

guards.why: What the ETL corpus contains, and how the run that produced it went. Everything below is judged against the newest one.

Two stores of the same table must have the same columns. The volume's funding_instruments had no `tier` while the laptop's did -- the volume had run 9 of the 23 committed migrations -- and because the census reads `tier`, a missing COLUMN was reported for half a day as a coverage LOSS. It runs here rather than in CI because it is a question about LIVE stores, and it runs inside the container so the corpus it reads is the one the cron actually writes.
Liveness must not reach the headline figures, and must move the offerable set. It was in CI, where data/db.sqlite is gitignored, so it printed 'skipping' and returned 0 on every run it has ever had.
A country's offerable inventory falling with no corresponding corpus change. Already a cron step; publishing its verdict is what makes the result readable without credentials.

Did the run that built this corpus finish every step it started. The other guards ask what the corpus CONTAINS and whether its schema is right; a half-refreshed corpus answers both perfectly well, and the coverage gate passed three censuses in a row that describe runs which failed. The outcome of a run is a property of the corpus that run produced, and it was being kept in a different store from the corpus -- so it did not survive `make pull-db`, and a partial volume became a publishable-looking laptop corpus with nothing left to say otherwise. The mark now lives in db.sqlite and travels with the file.
The committed fund snapshot against live Postgres: liveness agreement, profile coverage, and whether the semantic cache every NO_PG check ranks on is the real index.
The two stores must produce the same brief. Every other check runs NO_PG=1, so the whole suite is green regardless of what Postgres holds.
No fund a founder is shown on the fallback corpus may be one the live register says has closed. Measured at 26% of founders before the policy landed.

Does retrieval still find the fund a company actually won. Skips itself without credentials and exits 0, so a ranking change has always been able to merge with the floors never evaluated. The fingerprint above is what closes that.

No published `who may apply` block may state a population that cannot apply. Five did when this guard was found on 2026-08-08: two Latvian guarantee schemes the borrower's bank submits, an Innovasjon Norge row whose text was a cluster-programme paragraph its own recorded source never asserted, a closed English risk-finance scheme delivered through financial intermediaries, and an Irish community scheme applied for by registered project coordinators. A founder matched on any of them spends the effort and is rejected at the end, which is worse than never being shown the fund. It says FAILS THE BUILD in its own header and had been wired into nothing since the day it was written.

Everything the advisor may state, it must be able to retrieve. 954 of 5,804 attributable gates across 163 instruments were unembedded when this was found on 2026-08-08, and the shape matters more than the number: this guard was step 16 of ETL/refresh.py, the two embed steps that fix it were 14 and 15, and step 13 was red -- so the fix sat under the failure and the alarm sat under the fix. Registered here it is asserted weekly by check_verdicts.ts without depending on a 23-step chain reaching it. It reads Postgres only and costs nothing; the embed steps it reports on are the paid ones.

suite_accepted.$why:
The same arrangement as `accepted` above, one layer out: that block covers the eleven guards that need credentials and publish verdicts, this one covers the sixty checks `npm run check` runs. It exists because on 2026-08-18 thirteen of them were red on main and seven had been red since 2026-08-12 -- 139 consecutive commits -- and not one of the thirteen was distinguishable from the others. A defect, a guard grading the wrong subject, and a corpus-state fact that only a republish can fix take OPPOSITE work, and an undifferentiated red block is why three separate agents read past all thirteen in one day. 

An entry says which of the three it is (`class`), who it belongs to (`owner`), the day it went red (`since`), the failure it covers (`failure`, a regex the check's own last line must match) and when the decision expires (`review`). The bindings are enforced in website/frontend/scripts/lib/acceptance.ts, which check_verdicts.ts reads too -- one definition of what 'already decided' means, not two. On top of the four that block already enforces, a suite acceptance is capped: `review` may be at most MAX_HELD_DAYS after `since`, because a hold that outlives the silence it is holding is the silence with a date on it. 

It is not a mute button and it is not a place to put today's inconvenience. It fails the build when the check goes green (an acceptance that outlives what it accepted is pre-authorisation for the next regression), when the check starts failing a different way, when the review date passes, and when it names a check the suite does not run. Held failures are PRINTED IN FULL on every run of `npx vitest run`.

suite_tiers.$why:
WHO EXPERIENCES THIS FAILURE? Every check in `npm run check` answers it here, before it may be added. 

The suite went from 0 checks on 14 July to 59 on 18 August -- 49 of them in two weeks -- and on the day it reached 59, THIRTEEN were red on main and seven had been red across 139 consecutive commits. Every one of the 59 was individually justified when it was written. That is exactly how a suite outgrows attention: nothing ever asked what a failure would cost, so every check arrived at the same severity as every other, and a founder-facing defect and a stale markdown tag went red in the same colour. Thirteen reds printed as one block is what taught three separate agents to read past all thirteen in a single day. 

So there are two tiers and the difference is the BUILD: 
  founder -- a person is handed something wrong if this fails: a row that should not be there, a row that should be and is not, a dead link, a name that is a database key, a number on the page the corpus does not hold, a memo cut off mid-sentence. These FAIL the build. 
  report  -- true, and nobody is harmed today. It grades an internal artifact, a harness, a measurement's honesty, or a ratchet on debt. These are RUN and RECORDED and PRINTED on every run, and they do not fail anything. 

`protects` is required and is prose, not a category: one sentence naming what a person would experience, or -- for a report -- what it watches and who reads it. A tier with no sentence is refused, because the sentence is the work. If you cannot write it for a new check, that is the check telling you it should not fail a build. 

`report` is NOT a mute button and not somewhere to put an inconvenient red. A report-tier check that goes red is still recorded in data/check_status.json and still printed in full, every run. What it does not do is stop a branch that touched nothing it watches. Moving a check from founder to report is a decision about who gets hurt, and it belongs in a commit message that says so.

a red check is owned.protects: The suite's own attention. It fails vitest when a check is stale or red with nobody's name on it -- read by whoever is about to push.

typecheck.protects: A type error ships a broken page or a route that throws mid-brief.

unit tests.protects: The eligibility evaluator, the request sanitiser and watch-only detection: every one of them decides what a founder is shown.

segment config is a literal.protects: A non-literal revalidate makes Next serve a page from a cache nobody can reason about, so a founder reads figures from an unknown vintage.

output contracts.protects: The memo's own spec. A rule declared enforced and not routed is a promise the brief breaks in front of the person reading it.

a contract states no rate.protects: A prompt stating a frequency the code does not compute makes the brief assert a confident falsehood about the founder's own odds.

a euro figure says what it is a quantity.protects: Four different bases were printed to the writer as four bare numbers and it matched them, so the founder read the wrong money.

a rule's check can actually run.protects: Whether a rule's decider is reachable from a request. It grades the contract wiring rather than an output; check_contracts and the unit tests catch what a founder would feel.

rendered numbers.protects: A number on the three pages a visitor reads that the corpus does not produce. The visitor IS the founder.

published figures.protects: The owner's own planning document, project-mgmt/RESUME_HERE.md. Real -- it found four unsourced figures being planned on today -- but no founder reads that file, and a build failure over a markdown tag is precisely what taught people that red means nothing.

a measured ceiling was raised.protects: A max_tokens ceiling measured to bind and left in force truncates the brief, and the founder reads a memo that stops mid-sentence.

sector evidence.protects: An AI company was published a film and television scheme. This is the check that would have stopped it.

a funds: line states a scope.protects: A candidate row whose scope line says nothing. The ranker was handed the won fund nine times and took it zero times, and not one of those nine rows carried a usable line.

vocabulary contract.protects: An intake option no fund in the corpus can match: the founder answers and the answer deletes their pool.

a comparator asks the rule's question.protects: The founder answers truthfully and loses a fund that admits them, because the comparator decides on a question their answer cannot determine.

one env loader.protects: Whether a HARNESS declares the credentials it reads. It protects the honesty of measurements, not a founder's memo -- a harness that ranks lexically prints a number that misleads the owner, one step removed from anybody's brief.

client/server boundary.protects: A client module reaching pg is a page that throws in the founder's browser.

payload budget.protects: The per-request payload. Past budget the request slows and then fails, mid-brief.

both stores select the same columns.protects: A column the fallback does not carry. check_hydration_parity is the stronger version of the same question and IS founder-tier; this is its hermetic subset.

every archetype gets a table.protects: An archetype was receiving ZERO ROWS -- a founder shown no table at all -- while the guard above it reported passing.

liveness has one definition.protects: Two definitions of 'is this fund open' is how a scheme that ended in 2020 reached a real founder as row 5 of seven.

openness is evidenced.protects: A row asserting openness on no deadline we hold. The founder is sent to a door we cannot say is open.

no door is offered on an expired fact.protects: The calibration case: a real founder was published a scheme that ended 2020-12-30, with a link and an award figure.

offer routes are sourced.protects: A row that is not an offer -- nothing a founder can apply to -- presented as one.

a row is named by something outside its.protects: Twelve rows named after the loader's own partition keys were in founders' pools; Poland's ENTIRE pool was eight of them.

a displayed name is not an id.protects: A real founder read the row label 'rnd sa 111728 ministere de l economie et des finances'.

capital kinds match the register.protects: G and DG were transposed and the corpus held zero guarantees from a feed publishing 17,023 of them. A whole kind of capital silently missing from every founder's table.

regions match NUTS.protects: A region the classification does not hold makes every regional rule there unevaluable, so the founder's own region stops separating anything.

theme index is not stale.protects: An instrument indexed on stale tokens falls under the relevance floor and stops being offered, with nothing to notice it by. 180 of 1,088 were stale on 2026-08-18.

selector's base rate is current.protects: The base rate the selector IS TOLD. A stale curve makes the prompt state a confident falsehood about the list in front of the model.

leaf cap headroom.protects: A channel/country group past the cap loses leaves from the founder's pool silently.

missing-data neutral.protects: The stand-in for a fund with no history. The constant this replaced sat at the 79th percentile, so every historyless fund was being flattered into founders' tables.

capital reach.protects: An intake answer that reaches no publishable fund: the founder answers and gets nothing back.

a filter can admit someone.protects: Inert comparators -- filters no answer can satisfy either way. By construction they block nobody, so no founder experiences one; it is an encoder-health ratchet and the encoder owner reads it.

open questions still cover the corpus.protects: Requirements with no judgement are never offered as a question. Real, and diffuse: it is a coverage ratchet whose only fix is a paid classification pass, so it belongs in a report and not in a branch's build.

a winner is never screened out.protects: The TERRITORIAL screen, which is not shipped -- this guard is the reason it is not. It grades code no founder reaches; its shipped twin is the line below.

a winner is never gated out of the memo.protects: The same property on the stage that DOES ship. It was deleting the won fund for 62% of the answer key until the comparator learned that 'Denmark' and 'DK' are one country.

asking a question never costs a fund.protects: The owner's binding decision: a second-screen answer informs the ranker and never removes a fund. `accessiblePool` is the one seam that removes.

recall set does not leak.protects: A leaked answer key makes every published figure describe a product that does not exist, and the roadmap those figures set is what founders eventually get.

request path cannot reach the answer.protects: A founder's own request reaching the answer key. The key sits in the directory the memo path imports from.

harness answers as the founder.protects: Whether a replay harness answered the intake on the founder's behalf. It grades a measurement, not an output -- but it is why every EXACT@5 this repo published had usedInField false on every row.

peer prior canary.protects: A regenerated peer prior cost ten graded cases. It watches a measurement input; the owner reads it.

quotations match documents.protects: A quotation shown to a founder that its document does not contain would be founder-tier -- but data/raw/instrument_docs is gitignored, so this SKIPS everywhere except a machine holding the corpus. A check that skips is not a check, and pretending otherwise is the false green this repo keeps paying for.

dependency audit.protects: A high or critical advisory in what the site serves.

country gates.protects: A positive country rule no founder answer can satisfy hides its fund from everyone. One such rule is live today and it is deleting real winners.

gate field reach.protects: An answer we collect that never arrives at the evaluator: the founder answers and the answer does nothing.

answers reach the ranker.protects: The other half. Four answers were lost in the gap between reach and use in one week.

answers reach the writer.protects: No model ranks today, so the writer is the de facto selector, and the founder-facts block had lost seven intake fields including sector, useOfFunds and region.

gate pertinence.protects: An unjudged gate can still decide a verdict. That is the exact state the IPCEI gates were in when they wrongly unpublished a fund.

applicant identity.protects: Published 'who may apply' prose describing a population that cannot in fact apply. The founder is told to knock on a door only a bank may open.

corpus currency.protects: The two corpora disagreeing about which funds are open. 26% of founders served off the snapshot were shown at least one fund whose deadline had passed; on Postgres, 0%.

site serves the ETL's corpus.protects: The headline figures a visitor reads on the home page against the corpus the ETL actually holds.

degradation policy.protects: Every fund offered off the fallback corpus must be one the live register still calls open.

both stores agree.protects: The founder's own table, built twice, from the two stores. A disagreement is a founder answered from whichever store the connection happened to reach.

recall floor.protects: The product's own floor: whether the fund a company actually won is in the pool, in the accessible set, and in the first five rows.

published verdicts.protects: The readout of every guard that needs credentials -- including the census, the currency guard and applicant identity. Without it those failures reach nobody at all.

suite_tiers.$why_cadence:
`cadence: weekly` takes a check OUT of the default `npm run check` and leaves it to `npm run check --deep`. Two checks -- `asking a question never costs a fund` (310s) and `recall floor` (196s) -- were 73% of a 690-second suite on 2026-08-18. A twelve-minute command that needs DATABASE_URL is a command people run at the end of a workstream, if at all, which is half of why thirteen reds went a week without a reader. Without them the suite is about three minutes. 

This is only safe BECAUSE of data/check_status.json: a weekly check's row still ages, and check_red_debt still fails `npx vitest run` once any row passes the 7-day cap. So taking a measurement off the fast path does not take it out of sight -- it converts 'nobody ran it' from something invisible into a build failure with the command to fix it printed beside the name.

every guard runs somewhere, or says why.protects: A check that runs nowhere automatic is not protecting anybody. It named SEVENTEEN modules on 2026-08-18, `check_dead_doors` among them — the guard built that week to stop a real founder being sent to a scheme that closed in 2020.

every committed artifact can be rebuilt.protects: A committed artifact with no provable producer cannot be rebuilt, so when it goes wrong there is nothing to regenerate it from. Real, and today's five are answer keys and pinned fixtures nobody is served from — it belongs in a report.

the cron can read what it imports.protects: The corpus of record. A cron step that reads a committed data/ path at import cannot start in the container — data/ is the mounted volume and git ignores the tree whole — and railway_cron.py exits on it, so the load, the classifier, the sanity check, both window refreshes and all four guards are skipped and the weekly refresh stops without a word. It stopped on 2026-08-16 and ran three more days before anybody asked why.
